error_reason: The Orchestrator mis-specified the task by instructing WebSurfer to retrieve 'the numbers needed to calculate the sample standard deviations' (or even precomputed SDs) directly from ScienceDirect, assuming such per-domain 2022 datasets or SDs were readily available. This incorrect framing led the agent to seek precomputed statistics and encounter captchas instead of planning to extract raw counts of Major Reference Works per subdomain from ScienceDirect’s 2022 pages and compute SDs locally. Because of this initial misinterpretation, no correct data collection or computation path was established, causing the final wrong answer. Correcting this step to specify collecting raw per-subdomain counts from ScienceDirect and computing the SDs would have prevented the failure.

hypotheses.rationale: The Orchestrator directed WebSurfer to 'retrieve the numbers needed to calculate the sample standard deviations' from ScienceDirect, implicitly assuming such per-domain datasets and their 2022 counts are directly available on ScienceDirect. The task requires using ScienceDirect to obtain the counts per Life Sciences subdomains and Health Sciences subdomains and then compute sample standard deviations and their difference. By not specifying the concrete path on ScienceDirect (e.g., Elsevier Major Reference Works catalog by domain in 2022, list extraction, and computing SD) and instead framing it as fetching 'sample standard deviations' or statistics, it set the run on a path to search for precomputed SDs or external analyses. This mis-specification caused immediate derailment to JSTOR/contacts and ultimately failure.
